title: reassemble() partial result: data from missing-part collection has undefined byte layout
description: When parts are missing, reassemble() returns Ok with is_truncated=true and data containing the concatenation of only the *present* parts decoded in ascending order. The returned data has no documented relationship to the byte offsets of the original file — it is not a sparse buffer, it is not a per-part Vec<Option<...>>, it is a compact concatenation of whatever happened to be present. A caller cannot use this data to reconstruct the file even if they later obtain the missing part because they don't know where to splice it in. The API surface (ReassembledFile::data as Vec<u8>) makes this look like valid file data. The is_truncated flag and missing_parts list warn the caller the data is corrupt, but the data field itself is misleadingly typed. Consider: (a) returning data as Option<Vec<u8>> (None when truncated), or (b) returning Vec<Option<Vec<u8>>> per-part, or (c) documenting explicitly that partial data is only useful for diagnostics and must never be written to disk as a complete file.
